newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- JSE president Roy Andersen has been chosen as heir apparent to Liberty Life Association of Africa Ltd group CE and founder Donald Gordon, who says he plans to relinquish his executive role in the 31 billion rand life group.
- Government is experiencing a revenue bonanza this fiscal year which is likely to offset any overspending, figures released Thursday night suggest.
- British Aerospace has acquired a minority stake in Midrand-based Advanced Technologies & Engineering (ATE) in the biggest European/SA aerospace industry partnership yet.

- President Nelson Mandela sent an urgent fax to Zambian President Frederick Chiluba on Thursday asking him to postpone next week's poll - even if it meant declaring a state of emergency - to enable former president Kenneth Kaunda to contest the election.
- Dismissed Free State premier Patrick Lekota would be redeployed to the Senate in a bid to bring the vicious power struggle in the province to an end, President Nelson Mandela said Thursday.
- Roy Andersen, the outgoing executive president of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, will join the Liberty Life Group as heir apparent to Donald Gordon, Liberty said on Thursday.
- Doctors and pharmacies may be forced to change a flat dispensing fee of 20 rand if the parliamentary portfolio committee on health gets its way.
- South African Breweries Ltd management is considering unbundling its non-core assets, which involve not just beer but a broader definition of beverage-related assets.
